analysis.investment_thesis: GKSL scores well on capital efficiency (ROCE ~51%) but catastrophically fails the earnings yield test at ~2% (EBIT INR 17 Cr / EV ~INR 823 Cr), making the Magic Formula rank it near the bottom of any screener. You're paying 20x revenue and 90x earnings for a INR 40 Cr revenue hospital — the price completely negates the business quality.
key_strengths: High ROCE of 51.5% — suggests strong capital efficiency in specialty healthcare
Rapid revenue ramp: 0 → 5 → 40 Cr in three years shows real operational traction
High promoter holding (71.45%) aligns founder incentives with business growth
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~2% (EBIT 17 Cr / EV 823 Cr) — far below the Magic Formula's 12% minimum threshold
Tiny revenue base (INR 40 Cr) with INR 805 Cr market cap; any execution stumble destroys the valuation story
Negative FCF in FY2025 (-5 Cr) despite reported profits signals heavy reinvestment or working capital strain
red_flags: Data anomaly: EBITDA of INR 18-22 Cr in FY2023-24 when revenue was 0-5 Cr — this is arithmetically impossible and signals data reliability concerns
P/S of 13x and P/B of 22x for a small-cap hospital company are speculative-grade multiples with zero margin of safety
Free cash flow turned negative (-5 Cr) in FY2025 despite INR 10 Cr net profit — earnings quality is questionable
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT (operating income) = INR 17 Cr for FY2025. Enterprise Value = Market Cap (805.4) + Total Debt (23) – Cash (5) ≈ INR 823 Cr. Earnings Yield = 17/823 = **2.1%** — this is five times below the 12% floor I require and roughly six times below the 15% I get excited about. On the ROIC side, the story is better: reported ROCE of 51.5% and capital employed of roughly INR 54 Cr (equity 34 + borrowings 20) gives EBIT/Capital of ~31%, which is genuinely excellent for a specialty hospital. But the Magic Formula requires **both** metrics to rank high, and a 2% earnings yield immediately drops this to the bottom decile.

The financial data also raises serious red flags. EBITDA was reported as INR 18-22 Cr in FY2023-24 when revenue was essentially zero — this is internally inconsistent and could reflect accounting reclassifications, stub-period reporting, or data sourcing errors from a recently-listed micro-cap. Revenue only reached INR 40 Cr in FY2025 yet the company trades at INR 805 Cr — a 20x revenue multiple typical of high-growth SaaS, not a regional specialty hospital. Even if the business doubles revenue two more times, the current price embeds a decade of perfection. Pass.
